1 (Currently amended): A catheter system for delivering ultrasonic energy to a treatment site within a body lumen, the catheter comprising: a tubular body having a proximal end, a distal end and an energy delivery section positioned between the proximal end and the distal end; a plurality of ultrasound radiating members positioned within the energy delivery section, the plurality of ultrasound radiating members being allocated into electrical groups comprising more than one ultrasound radiating member; wherein the ultrasound radiating members of one electrical group are spatially interdigitated with the ultrasound radiating members of another electrical group, and wherein the ultrasound radiating members are interdigitated in a unique pattern different from an exclusively regular or pseudo random pattern.

4 (Currently amended): The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the ultrasound radiating members are interdigitated in a unique pattern that differentiates from known regular and pseudo random patterns.

5 (Currently amended): The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the ultrasound radiating members are interdigitated in a unique arrangement such that no two interdigitated ultrasound radiating members align perfectly in a repetitive sequence. 

6 (Currently amended): A system for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the system comprising: a first and a second ultrasound catheter, each of the first and the second ultrasound catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion; the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section having at least one ultrasound element; the tubular body also including at least one fluid delivery lumen; and a control system configured to operate both the first and the second ultrasound catheters.

7 (Currently amended): The system of Claim 6, wherein the control system operates both the first and the second ultrasound catheters simultaneously.

8 (Currently amended): The system of Claim 7, wherein the control system is configured to independently control the ultrasound radiating members on the first and the second ultrasound catheters.

11 (Currently amended): An ultrasound catheter for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the catheter comprising: a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion; the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section comprising at least one ultrasound element and at least one fluid delivery lumen; the tubular body defining a guidewire lumen extending through the proximal portion and the ultrasound energy delivery section and further extending beyond the distal portion.
